messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a memory regression on staging after the recent allocator change (reduce-frag branch). Smallalloc benchmark OOMed at ~48s. Leaving repro steps here, can someone run a quick heapshot/bench and share artifacts?

maya: Repro snippet:```
git checkout reduce-frag
make -j8 bench-smallalloc
REDWOOD_BENCH_OPTS=\"--iters 1000 --seq 1024\" ./bin/smallalloc-bench --threads=32
```

maya: Pattern: RSS creeping steadily then sudden +1.2GB jump and OOM. We didn't see this on main. Suspect slab packing or arena growth.

sam: I can run a couple of reproductions. Do you have the exact commit sha? Also which instance type in staging?

maya: sha: f3a2c9d. Staging uses r-infer-staging-gpu-2 (32G). I observed it on 2/3 runs.

sam: OK starting a run now. Will grab heapshots and jemalloc stats. If it dies, I’ll attach /proc/$PID/smaps and jemalloc stats.

bench-bot: run queued: bench-smallalloc (id: 1805004321-1). Alloc profile will be uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/1805004321/ when finished.

sam: First run completed (no OOM) — RSS peaked ~2.1GB. Starting longer run with --iters=5000.

infra-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/1805004321/run-2/jemalloc_stats.txt

sam: Attached snippet from jemalloc_stats (run-2):
```
active:   2310144000
mapped:   2440000000
retained: 0
arenas:  6 active
arena_decay: disabled
```

kevin: Can you dump arenas info? I'm curious whether the new per-thread arena behavior left many partially-used slabs.

sam: dumping now: /tmp/arena-dump-1805004321.txt (uploaded). Preliminary: multiple arenas with many small footprints in the 64K/256K sizeclasses.

olivia: Quick thought — the change reduced fragmentation by avoiding merges, but might have increased retained pages due to less compaction. Could be interacting with our KV cache growth pattern. Any recent kv-cache rollout?

maya: We did increase kv-cache window last week (cache-window=2h) in staging to test hit-rate. Might be correlated.

leah: I can try a run with kv-cache disabled to isolate. If RSS stabilizes with cache off, that points to cross-slab interactions.

sam: Run with cache off queued. Also enabling MALLOC_CONF=abort:0,lg_chunk:22 so we can get better backtraces on OOM.

ben ch-bot: run complete (id: 1805004321-3) — no OOM with kv-cache disabled; RSS peaked ~1.9GB.

maya: Interesting. So KV cache increases working set and maybe changes allocation patterns enough to expose fragmentation.

kevin: Suggestion: try forcing arena reuse: export MALLOC_CONF=\"narenas:2,percpu_arena:0\" and re-run. If that reduces retained amount it's arena count related.

sam: Running with narenas=2 now. Also capturing pprof heap profile: `./bin/smallalloc-bench --pprof heap.prof` and uploading.

infra-bot: pprof uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/1805004321/heap.prof.gz

sam: pprof shows a lot of allocations from kv-cache chunk allocation path: kv::prefix_cache::alloc_chunk at ~42% of live bytes.

olivia: That aligns — allocator change may avoid merging small frees causing many isolated chunks to stay in separate slabs. For short-term mitigation we can do: 1) lower kv-cache window, 2) set narenas low. Long-term we need either a slab coalescer or periodic shrinker.

maya: I filed a quick mitigation PR to set cache-window=30m in staging and to set MALLOC_CONF=narenas:4 in deployment manifest: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/8345 — please review.

kevin: Reviewed. :thumbsup: Also adding a runtime flag to trigger a background slab-scan would help. I'll open a design issue.

leah: Thanks — I'll run a few more stress runs overnight with the new config and paste results tomorrow. If we still see edge OOMs we'll consider reverting the allocator change until we have a scavenger.

maya: Appreciate the quick triage. If anyone finds a simple heapshot that shows fragmentation distribution (bytes per arena/sizeclass) paste it here.

sam: Will follow up with CSV of sizeclass retention by arena in the morning.

kevin: For visibility — adding @eng-sre and @eng-platform to the thread.

maya: :heart:
